---
title: "Concentration-response modelling"
subtitle: "Estimating no-effect toxicity values from concentration-response data in R"
---

Estimates of no-effect toxicity underpin both risk assessment and the derivation
of environmental quality standards. A range of statistical approaches developed
or adopted in ecotoxicology over the past decade have changed how those
estimates are obtained from concentration-response experiments, and this course
covers the current methods for deriving them in R.

The material begins with concentration-response modelling itself: the difference
between linear, non-linear and threshold models, the natural scale of a response
variable and what follows from it for the choice of statistical distribution,
and the distinction between the toxicity metrics that can be derived from a
fitted curve. It then introduces the no-significant-effect concentration (NSEC),
and works through fitting and interpretation using `bayesnec`, which fits these
models in a Bayesian framework via `brms` and Stan. Model averaging is treated
throughout rather than as an addition, because a single equation chosen from a
candidate set rarely carries the evidence a guideline value needs.

## Course outcomes

On completing the material you will be able to:

- distinguish linear, non-linear and threshold concentration-response models,
  and say which is appropriate for a given endpoint;
- identify the statistical distribution appropriate to a response variable, and
  fit a generalised model accordingly;
- fit concentration-response models in R and plot the results;
- derive NEC, NSEC and ECx estimates, and explain what each of them measures;
- apply model averaging across a candidate set, and interpret the weights;
- produce complete workflows for estimating no-effect toxicity suitable for use
  in species sensitivity distribution derivation.

## Modules

Before the modules: [software setup](vignettes/0Software-setup.qmd) installs R,
a C++ compiler, CmdStan and the R packages, and verifies the installation. It is
not taught; it is done beforehand.

| | Module | Subject |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [The software stack](vignettes/1Software-stack.qmd) | R, Stan, `brms` and `bayesnec`, and Positron |
| 2 | [Fitting a single model](vignettes/2Fitting-a-CR-model-using-bayesnec.qmd) | the `bnec` call, the fitted object, plotting |
| 3 | [Toxicity estimation and the model set](vignettes/3Toxicity_estimation_and_available_models.qmd) | NEC, NSEC and ECx, and the available equations |
| 4 | Model averaging and multi-model inference | candidate sets, weights, averaged estimates |
| 5 | Response data and statistical distributions | matching the family to the endpoint |
| 6 | Priors and Bayesian inference | default priors, checking them, changing them |
| 7 | A worked case study | herbicide toxicity, start to finish |
| 8 | Factor covariates and groupings | comparing curves and estimates across groups |

Modules 4 to 8 are being converted from the earlier version of this course and
are linked here as they are completed. A frequentist treatment of the same
material using `drc` is supplied separately as reference; it is not part of the
taught sequence.

## Working through the material independently

The modules are written to be read in order and are self-contained. Each shows
the code that produced every result on the page, so the reasoning can be
followed without running anything.

Fitting Bayesian concentration-response models takes time. A single model may
take minutes and a model-averaged set considerably longer, so the larger fits in
these modules are shown with their code and their output rather than being run
as you read. Anything that runs quickly is intended to be run.

If you want to run the code yourself, work through the [software
setup](vignettes/0Software-setup.qmd) first. It installs R, a C++ compiler,
CmdStan and the R packages, and ends with a script that verifies the
installation.

## Workshop participants

This material is taught as a full-day workshop at SETAC Australasia 2026.

The [software setup](vignettes/0Software-setup.qmd) is pre-work and must be
completed beforehand. No time is set aside on the day to install or repair
software, and a participant without a working installation will be able to
follow the demonstrations but not fit models alongside them.

## Source and citation

The material is developed at the [Australian Institute of Marine
Science](https://www.aims.gov.au/) and the source is at
[open-AIMS/cr_modelling_training](https://github.com/open-AIMS/cr_modelling_training).

`bayesnec` is documented at
[open-aims.github.io/bayesnec](https://open-aims.github.io/bayesnec/). The NSEC
is introduced in Fisher and Fox (2023), *Environmental Toxicology and
Chemistry*.

Corrections and questions are welcome as
[issues](https://github.com/open-AIMS/cr_modelling_training/issues).
